Coverage denominators and unresolved references remain explicit. Partition axes cannot be added together; eligible supersession is assertion-specific. exit_state: Chapter 3 is complete through physical 73. Literal source, supported interpretation and event-specific accounting permission remain separate. JPMorgan's 156 reference is retained as text but rejected as the report start; 163 is the supported navigation target, with no observed human decision. Coverage has three populations; nearest-rounding bounds require an admitted assumption. Public cutoff K and possession cutoff S filter different facts before revision selection. Bank commitment and insurance treaty corrections illustrate targeted supersession, candidate-population dependencies and complete-ancestry invalidation. Equal terminal cash cannot validate earlier recognition. Correcting an explanation does not alter committed journals; unsupported correction treatment creates no journal. Chapter 4 must now explain the distinct meanings of uncertainty in these retained alternatives.
findings: No new confirmed defect on actual rendered physical pages 68–73.

equation.symbols_units_domain: m is the displayed integer, s the positive monetary scale and y the underlying amount in the scaled currency units; the 100-million example fixes their interpretation.
equation.assumptions_timing: Nearest rounding is explicitly admitted, not established for Apple; no temporal premise or stochastic measure enters the enclosure.
equation.source_and_equality: Correct local enclosure under nearest rounding: dividing by positive s gives distance from integer m no more than one half; unknown ties motivate conservative closed endpoints.
equation.interpretation: The retained value may differ from the displayed centre by half a displayed unit under this assumption; positive truncation yields a different one-sided interval.
equation.transition: The 99.5–100.5 versus 100–101 example and no-rule disposition prevent promoting the enclosure into an issuer fact; no executable computation or probability claim follows.
